admin-accounting-ads.name: Admin Accounting Ads Log
admin-accounting-ads.description: Superuser tracks advertising spend at /panel/accounting/ads: chronological list with a computed running accumulated column (calculated over the full history), origin-card and platform filters, saved filter tabs (accounting_ads view with seeded defaults) and modal CRUD; the leading three-dots menu of each row offers Detalle e historial, Ver nota when the record has a note, Editar and Eliminar with confirmation.

admin-accounting-card-catalog.name: Admin Accounting — Credit Card Catalog
admin-accounting-card-catalog.description: Superuser manages the CreditCard catalog from the 'Catálogo de tarjetas' section at /panel/accounting/settings: per-row name, cupo (credit_limit), 'extractos desde' month and active toggle, with per-row save (POST /api/accounting/credit-cards/create/ or PATCH .../update/) and delete with confirm (DELETE .../delete/ returns credit_card_referenced when snapshots/statements reference the name — deactivate instead). Saved cards lead with a three-dots menu (Detalle e historial fed with the stored card, Ver nota, Eliminar); unsaved drafts only discard inline. The catalog feeds the Tarjetas form dropdown, the server-side debt computation (cupo − disponible) and the Extractos year/month range; changes are audited as the credit_card entity.

admin-accounting-cards.name: Admin Accounting Card Snapshots
admin-accounting-cards.description: Superuser manages weekly credit-card balance snapshots at /panel/accounting/cards: list with latest-debt-per-card chip, filters (date range, debt range, card multi-select), create via modal (date defaults to today, card picked from a dropdown fed by the CreditCard catalog; the Deuda input is gone — debt is server-computed as cupo − disponible and previewed in the form, which blocks disponible > cupo), edit prefill (legacy names outside the catalog injected as an extra option) and delete with ConfirmModal. Registering a snapshot dated on/after the cycle Friday silences the weekly card-debt email reminder. The card filter defaults to the active catalog cards as removable chips (clearing them surfaces historical names); its options are the union of catalog and snapshot names, and a saved tab in the URL wins over the preselection. Row actions follow the panel standard: a leading three-dot menu with no visible header opens a modal with Detalle e historial, Editar and Eliminar. The Notas column no longer prints the note: it shows a 'Ver nota' button (or '—' when empty) that opens the full note in a modal, with the active search highlighted. At phone and portrait widths the visible columns fill the table with no blank band and the table fits without horizontal scroll.

admin-accounting-collection-context.name: Admin Accounting Collection Account Context
admin-accounting-collection-context.description: Asocia una cuenta de proyecto a contrato y otrosí opcional del mismo contrato, o al único hosting, con razón, control de versión y validación de coherencia; conserva snapshot, PDF, importes y pagos.

admin-accounting-collection-create.name: Admin Accounting Cuenta de Cobro Create + Preview
admin-accounting-collection-create.description: Superuser creates a cuenta de cobro from the Cuentas de cobro tab button or from an income row action (kind expected/liquid, never lost; incomes with an active cuenta are blocked and expose a Ver cuenta de cobro navigation instead). The modal unifies with the clients module (ClientAutocomplete prefills the canonical billing_customer projection with legal name, NIT/cedula, identification type, contact, real email and address into the document snapshot; inline client creation without leaving the flow), requires selecting an income via searchable combobox — or creating the expected income inline via the stacked income form. The combobox asks for the whole eligible ledger once (no client param) and narrows it on the page through two chip groups above the search box, each option carrying its own count: Alcance (Del cliente, the default once a client is picked and literally only their rows / Todos, the way to reach the still-unassigned incomes and the ones filed under someone else) and Estado (Todos / Esperados / Líquidos). Estado always opens and resets to Esperados — including after changing clients — because a cuenta normally bills money that has not been collected; this is a stable default, never remembered from the prior modal use. The cut is by income kind, not payment status, so a partially paid expected income stays visible for its outstanding balance. Because the filtering is client-side the counts are exact and switching a chip costs no request, so the dropdown stays open and the cursor stays in the search box; the chips narrow the set the concept search then runs over. Under Todos the rows split into De {cliente} / De otros clientes (each naming its owner) / Sin cliente, with the unassigned ones selectable on purpose — issuing adopts the client onto them, announced under the field before the send. A combination with no rows names itself («Acme Soluciones no tiene ingresos esperados.»); «Ver todos (N)» first removes the Estado cut while preserving Del cliente, and only falls back to widening Alcance when that client has no eligible income at all, instead of rendering a blank panel that reads as a failed load. The list also closes on click-outside or Esc. Each group still declares how many rows it holds back; pairing an income with a different client raises an inline warning that blocks the preview until it is resolved, suggests an editable per-client consecutivo PA-{CODE}-{NNN} (sent only when edited), and ends in a mandatory step-2 preview rendering the REAL email subject/body and attached PDF (same backend pipeline as the send, rolled back server-side) side by side in a full-height two-column review with a draggable divider, independent scroll per column and a fixed header/footer, collapsing into Correo/PDF tabs below 1024px (opening on the PDF under 640px), before Confirmar y enviar issues, emails and links the document to the income. Marking an expected-linked cuenta as paid opens the same unified Liquidar ingresos modal, with inherited IVA, participations, deductions, optional hosting periods and an in-modal payment-confirmation review; it previews and submits through the shared grouped-settlement contract, even for this one income; a fully-settled income auto-marks its cuenta paid backend-side. Since Aug 2026 that modal also offers to complete the covered period when the income being settled is a hosting charge that never recorded one — proposed on the charge's own date, with the end computed from the periodicity picked, written to the expected income and never a condition: left untouched, the settlement goes through just the same (settling a hosting used to be refused outright over a period no screen in this flow could fill). Since Aug 2026 the Plazo de pago field accepts 0 — pago inmediato contra presentación — and a hint under the Ciudad/Plazo row says what that does (row help: a field hint inside an aligned row is never rendered), shown only while the days mode is active since a 0 means nothing beside a fecha fija. A zero term issues the cuenta with no due date, so neither the PDF nor the client email prints a vencimiento line at all (the label goes with it, and the dates block closes ranks rather than leaving a gap). Negative terms are refused by the input's min and by the serializer, and an emptied field still falls back to 8 (typed out-of-range values are clamped into 0–120 before the payload). Since Aug 2026 the step-2 PDF pane probes the served URL before mounting the viewer: a spinner while it resolves, the embed once it answers (the PDF endpoints ship X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN so the browser will render them framed at all), and on failure a panel in the app's own words pointing at Descargar / Abrir PDF — which keep working, so the review happens there and Confirmar y enviar stays available. Picking a hosting income that records the period it covers pre-fills the 'Período facturado' range instead of asking for it again. Since F7 (Aug 2026) a cuenta raised from a project-linked income lands in the list already showing that project: the draft inherits the income's project (kept in sync when the income's project changes later) and the Proyecto column reads the live FK. The income picker uses a modal-owned floating listbox outside the form's clipping panel, with the list as the only scrollbar while open. Since Aug 2026 a client whose selector row says Sin correo blocks preview with every missing prerequisite listed; the modal saves the canonical client email explicitly through PATCH and keeps the rest of the draft intact before continuing. Las cuentas nuevas de ingreso con proyecto exigen naturaleza exclusiva y contrato con otrosí opcional o hosting explícito; si hay suscripción se selecciona su obligación antes del preview. El servidor valida coherencia y el preview revierte todas las escrituras. IVA (2026-10): Hereda IVA del ingreso, acepta total incluido o base y muestra base, IVA y total en previsualización, PDF y correo. Antes de pagos, confirmar actualiza ingreso y cuenta juntos; previsualizar no persiste cambios. Con pagos o deducciones conserva tasa y saldo; documentos emitidos se corrigen anulando y reemitiendo. Formularios (2026-10-02): consecutivo y concepto comparten fila; valor, modo de captura e IVA forman un bloque propio sin columna vacía. «Editar ficha del cliente» guarda explícitamente la identidad y dirección canónicas, refresca los datos del documento y conserva el consecutivo manual y el borrador. «Cobro del proyecto» es visible también al entrar desde un ingreso; los errores indican si falta tipo de cobro, contrato, hosting o período. Volver de preview conserva la elección y cambiar de proyecto la limpia. Sin pagos, una tasa de ingreso no registrada propone 19%; un ingreso con pagos conserva tasa y saldo históricos. Contratos existentes (2026-10-06): desde Cobro del proyecto se registra explícitamente un documento del proyecto o contrato de una propuesta vinculada y se selecciona sin duplicar el original. Un rechazo conserva el formulario; cambiar de proyecto descarta respuestas de la consulta anterior. Último aviso (2026-10-09): «Confirmar y enviar» ya no envía; abre un último aviso con número, cliente, proyecto, concepto, valor total, fecha de emisión, vencimiento («Sin vencimiento» con plazo 0) y correo destinatario, leídos del mismo preview revertido. Sólo «Emitir y enviar» emite y envía; Esc o «Volver a revisar» cierran el aviso sin enviar y conservan el paso 2. Mientras envía, volver y reenviar quedan bloqueados. Un esperado completamente pagado que aún no tiene cuenta permanece elegible: el selector y el formulario usan el total íntegro del ingreso, no saldo cero. Al emitir esa cuenta, queda pagada sin crear otro movimiento ni pedir otro pago; el envío al cliente sigue siendo explícito.

admin-accounting-collection-detail.name: Collection Account Detail
admin-accounting-collection-detail.description: Superuser inspects one cuenta de cobro without leaving the tab: the row shows Cliente and Proyecto as separate columns, and the detail modal carries the linked income with its settlement history plus the emitted document in a Documento tab. Going to the income is the optional exit and must land on a tab that does not filter the focused row out. With a zero-day term there is no vencimiento, so the Emisión / Vence cell shrinks to Emisión over a single date instead of pairing it with an em-dash that reads as missing data. The Documento tab probes the inline PDF URL before embedding it — spinner while it resolves, and when the document cannot render, a message in the app's own words pointing at Descargar PDF instead of the browser's refused-connection page. El detalle permite asociar o corregir el contexto contractual o hosting del proyecto con motivo y versión; la corrección mantiene PDF, snapshot, importes y pagos. IVA (2026-10): El resumen muestra base, IVA registrado y total de la cuenta, además del desglose independiente del ingreso vinculado. Las cuentas de hosting también muestran IVA; un histórico sin tasa se distingue de Sin IVA. Si se emite después de que su esperado ya quedó Pagado, el detalle muestra la cuenta pagada y conserva el valor completo y el IVA del ingreso; no representa otro cobro.

admin-accounting-collection-grouping.name: Admin Accounting Collection Account Grouping
admin-accounting-collection-grouping.description: Superuser switches Cuentas de cobro between the classic table and a one-level grouped view, choosing Cliente or Proyecto. Each group shows its filtered row count; emitted (issued plus paid), pending (issued), collected (paid) and cancelled amounts; and draft, issued, overdue, paid and cancelled counts, with overdue intentionally overlapping issued. Groups order by pending descending with alphabetical ties and the unassigned bucket last. Snapshot-only projects remain distinct as historical groups, true blanks use Sin proyecto, and the footer totals exactly the filtered set. Both preferences are stored together in the global AccountingSettings singleton from either the page (immediate save with rollback on failure) or Configuracion, so a reload and another device see the last saved pair.

admin-accounting-collections.name: Admin Accounting Cuentas de Cobro Center
admin-accounting-collections.description: Superuser manages all cuentas de cobro at /panel/accounting/collections (tab renamed from Cobros): status counters (emitidas/pagadas/vencidas/anuladas with totals), segmented status filter, table with numero/origen (hosting/proyecto/ingreso/otro)/cliente/total/emision/vence/estado (Vencida tint via is_overdue) and row actions: view linked income, download PDF, resend to client, mark paid (expected-linked accounts route through the same unified settlement modal and shared preview/bulk-settle contract, with deductions, inherited IVA and payment confirmation reviewed inside that dialog), cancel (cancelling a hosting-linked account resumes its expiry notices; cancelling frees the linked income for a new cuenta). Since Aug 2026 Cliente and Proyecto are separate sortable, filterable columns and the row opens admin-accounting-collection-detail. Since Aug 2026 a cuenta issued with a zero-day payment term carries no due date at all: the Vence column stays empty and the row can never read as Vencida nor fall into that tab, because is_overdue derives from a date that no longer exists. Since Aug 2026 the row also offers eliminar, which is not anular: it removes the record physically and only appears when the backend says can_delete — the cuenta is already anulada, or it never reached the client (borrador, or emitida whose email failed). A pagada can be neither anulada nor eliminada. The confirmation names consecutivo, cliente and monto and demands the word ELIMINAR, because the delete is irreversible; the consecutivo is not reused (the series keeps a hole) and the linked income goes back to being billable. Every deletion leaves a DELETED row in the accounting historial naming the consecutivo that is gone. Since F7 (Aug 2026) the Proyecto column answers with the LIVE project relation (the FK the filter already matches on) and the frozen customer_project_name snapshot only fills FK-null legacy rows, so the cell and the project filter can never disagree; two cuentas of one client can honestly differ (one linked, one blank — the reported evidence case) and a reload tells the same truth. The frozen snapshot stays the PDF's truth, untouched. Classic and grouped rows now share one 44×44 leading three-dots action that opens CollectionActionsModal (first entry Detalle e historial; the internal notes open in the shared note dialog with its privacy hint), so no command is clipped at the trailing edge; compact columns fit 412 px without an inner horizontal scroll, while status, origin and unlinked-state badges stay atomic.

admin-accounting-dashboard.name: Admin Accounting Dashboard
admin-accounting-dashboard.description: Superuser opens /panel/accounting and sees the financial overview fed by GET /api/accounting/dashboard/?year=: expected vs liquid income, expenses, utilities and monthly breakdown computed from the company ledger only (personal-ledger records excluded), pocket balance, per-partner cards (Gustavo/Carlos combine company participation + personal ledger; ProjectApp (Empresa) shows the full company ledger totals), operative cost cards and latest card snapshots. The hero Utilidad líquida card embeds the full utility statistics surface as a default-open accordion with evolution, margin and partner tabs; the former 'Utilidad por mes' mini-chart, statistics icon and utility modal no longer exist. The hero grid aligns cards at their natural height to avoid blank space. The subnav orders Bolsillo second, after Resumen. The Contabilidad quick-access group replaces Ads with Cuentas de cobro linking to /panel/accounting/collections, while Ads remains in the internal accounting subnav. Includes the superuser gate: staff non-superusers are redirected to /panel and the Accounting sidebar section is hidden. Includes the Evolución section: two ApexCharts (expected vs liquid vs expenses per month, and card-debt evolution from snapshots) driven by the year selector plus a client-side month-range filter, a link to the cards history and the year persisted as a query param. Accounting charts use theme-aware foreground, legend, tooltip and center-label colors so their data remains readable in dark mode.

admin-accounting-empty-state-cta.name: Admin Accounting Lists — Empty State CTA
admin-accounting-empty-state-cta.description: With zero records, accounting lists render BaseEmptyState with a primary 'Nuevo <entidad>' action that opens the create modal; with active filters and zero matches the action becomes 'Limpiar filtros' and resets the filter panel.

admin-accounting-expenses-crud.name: Admin Accounting Expenses CRUD
admin-accounting-expenses-crud.description: Superuser manages expense records at /panel/accounting/expenses with category (Negocio/Personal) and ledger (Contabilidad) badges, partner split (hidden for personal-ledger expenses, which use a single Valor field) and the same modal CRUD + filters pattern as incomes; the leading three-dots menu of each row offers Detalle e historial, Ver nota when the record has a note, Editar and Eliminar with confirmation. Money inputs live-format es-CO thousands separators (BaseCurrencyInput). Since Jul 2026 the modal has a 'Registrar egreso en bolsillo' toggle (on by default): on creates/keeps a linked pocket OUT movement (bidirectional sync, edits/deletes mirror/cascade), off covers paper adjustments and expenses that never touched the pocket; a personal-ledger expense with the toggle on is stored as a company draw (ledger company, full split to the owner, warning hint in the modal) so pocket money always counts against company utility; on edit the toggle can link/unlink deliberately. Since Aug 2026 the period field captures the exact date by default ('Fecha', prefilled with today, shared PeriodDateField) with a toggle down to month-only ('Mes'); edits always open in full-date mode showing the stored day (01 for month-only records; the toggle still downgrades to month) and the backend already renders full dates as '17 Julio 2026'. Since Aug 2026 deductions are first-class in the tab: a 'Tipo de deducción' multi filter (shared catalog with the liquidation modal), Operativo/Deducciones chips over the filtered rows, a 'Deducciones (año)' KPI card with the per-type breakdown, the pill tooltip naming the origin income (source_income link), and the edit modal hiding the pocket toggle behind a hint for deduction rows — they are created from Liquidar only and reduce utility under the gross-income convention. IVA (2026-10): IVA opcional con 19% por defecto en gastos nuevos de cualquier contabilidad; editar conserva la tasa histórica, incluido 0 o null. «Sin IVA» permite elegir 0%: captura de total incluido o base antes del impuesto y desglose base/IVA/total en edición. No calcula IVA descontable ni cambia utilidad o reparto. Consulta individual desde el bolsillo: ?expense=<id> abre el gasto por ID independientemente de los filtros del listado, admite recarga y conserva su detalle e historial con estados de carga, error y registro inexistente.

admin-accounting-export.name: Admin Accounting Export
admin-accounting-export.description: Superuser exports accounting data: every list view has an Exportar dropdown (CSV / Excel .xlsx) that calls GET /api/accounting/export/ with the active filters mapped to server query params, and the dashboard has an Exportar Excel button that downloads the full workbook (summary sheet + one sheet per section) from /api/accounting/export/workbook/?year=.

admin-accounting-filters.name: Admin Accounting Filters
admin-accounting-filters.description: Superuser filters the incomes list client-side. Every dimension takes SEVERAL values at once (BaseSegmentedMulti, a role="group" of aria-pressed toggles): period date range, total amount min/max, Tipo (Esperado/Líquido/Pérdidas), Cobro (Sin pagos/Parcial/Pagado, mirroring the row payment badge), Socio, Contabilidad, plus the Cliente/Proyecto/Origen checkbox dropdowns, free-text search with debounce, active-filter count badge and reset. Values inside a dimension are OR'd and dimensions are AND'd — a hint line in the panel says so — and "Todos" clears the dimension rather than being a value in it. The applied-filter chip carries one entry per dimension listing the values chosen in it ("Cobro: Sin pagos, Parcial"), each removable on its own; a single-value dimension reads exactly as it always did. The landing tab "Esperados por cobrar" (id expected-pending) covers pending AND partial: as "Solo esperados" it meant pending only, so an expected income that had received an abono disappeared from the view that promises everything still uncollected. Tabs carry counts, and the active filters travel in the URL so a multi-value cut can be shared. Saved tabs keep a base_filters restore point: edits auto-save, a drifted tab shows a '•' and offers "Restaurar filtros" / "Fijar como base"; the drift comparison reads a scalar and its one-element array as the same cut, so tabs written before the move to multi-value do not report phantom drift. The strip is also reorderable: a chip is dragged to its place (hold to start on touch, so the strip can still be swiped), or moved from its own ⋯ menu ('Mover a la izquierda'/'Mover a la derecha') and with Ctrl/Cmd+arrows on the focused chip, which is the path for anyone who cannot drag. Dragging never applies the filter it moved. The order is per (user, view) and covers the factory presets too — a builtin's order rides a placeholder row matched by builtin_key, while its filters stay in the frontend — with 'Todas' pinned first because it sits outside the sortable list. 'Restablecer' in Configuración returns the whole strip to the factory order without touching the tabs the user saved.

admin-accounting-history-diagnosis.name: Admin Accounting History — Read and Retry a Send
admin-accounting-history-diagnosis.description: Superuser diagnoses a send from its own row in the Envíos subtab. The row's leading three-dots menu opens the message as it was delivered (GET accounting/email-log/<id>/body/, rendered in a sandboxed iframe via srcdoc like the branded-email composer); sends predating the feature say so instead of opening an empty modal. A failed send is retried from the row menu (POST accounting/email-log/<id>/retry/), reaching only the address on that row — the other recipients already got their copy. Only the notices tied to a single record (cambio contable, cuenta de cobro, pago de hosting, confirmación de pago al cliente y aviso interno de ingreso completo) are retryable; the three digests show the menu entry disabled carrying the reason, because re-running one would build today's summary rather than the message that failed. The disabled entry keeps its reason visible under its label, and opening the menu never expands the row. The retry lands as a new log row linked to the original through retry_of, so both attempts stay visible, and a retry that fails again reports its cause. The expanded row also names the records the email was about (EmailLogTarget). income_completed_account_pending se reintenta sólo a la dirección fallida, conserva retry_of y no vuelve a liquidar ni crea otro evento de completitud.

admin-accounting-history-filters.name: Admin Accounting History — Filters and Predefined Tabs
admin-accounting-history-filters.description: Superuser narrows the send log at /panel/accounting/history without rebuilding the filter by hand. Each subtab runs its own useAccountingFilters instance (views accounting_history_sends / accounting_history_changes) over the server-paginated endpoints, so the filter row translates into query params through buildExportParams instead of filtering loaded rows. Envíos filters by aviso, estado, tipo de registro, cliente, proyecto, acción de origen, destinatario, rango de fechas and free text over the subject; Cambios by entidad, acción, usuario, fecha and free text over the record name. Under the filter row sits the predefined strip (ProposalFilterTabs, the PA-44 standard): "Fallidos", "Hoy" and "Últimos 7 días" are builtin — a stored date would freeze on the day it was seeded, and Fallidos has to sit second — while "Recordatorios de cobro", "Cambios contables" and "Eliminaciones" are seeded rows that Configuración can restore. Every tab carries its count, "Todas" included and the (0) included, fetched from POST accounting/history/tab-counts/ because there are no loaded rows to count; what does not fit collapses into a "+N" menu that always hoists the selected tab back into view. Tab, filter row and chips move together: selecting a tab lights the controls, editing the controls un-lights a builtin, and "Limpiar filtros" deselects. The applied filters ride in the URL (only the visible subtab owns it), so a query can be bookmarked, shared, and reached directly from a hosting, an income or a cuenta de cobro through their "Ver correos de este registro" action. The active combination can be saved as an own tab, and Configuración administers the strip (visibility, order, and a Restablecer that keeps the own tabs).

admin-accounting-history.name: Admin Accounting History
admin-accounting-history.description: Superuser audits the accounting module at /panel/accounting/history through two subtabs, both server-paginated 20 per page. 'Cambios': change log (GET /api/accounting/change-logs/) with entity/action/actor/record/date filters and expandable field-level old→new diffs per entry. 'Envíos': send log (GET /api/accounting/email-log/) showing which recipients each automated email of the module actually reached — one row per address — with aviso/estado/destinatario/date filters plus the record, client, project and subject cuts. Both subtabs carry a predefined tab strip, own saved tabs and URL-persisted filters (admin-accounting-history-filters), and a send row can be read and retried (admin-accounting-history-diagnosis). Exporting either subtab as CSV/XLSX goes through the same filters as the list (admin-accounting-export). Envíos incluye “Ingreso completo — cuenta pendiente”: aviso interno creado al completar por primera vez un esperado de empresa sin cuenta emitida, con ingreso objetivo y estado real de entrega.

admin-accounting-hosting-billing.name: Admin Accounting Hosting — Enviar Cuenta de Cobro
admin-accounting-hosting-billing.description: Superuser sends a client the cuenta de cobro from a hosting row at /panel/accounting/hostings: the row menu's 'Enviar cuenta de cobro' entry (disabled with its reason without client email) opens a ConfirmModal previewing amount/recipient, POSTs /api/accounting/hostings/:id/send-collection-account/ which issues the Document (public number, one line item for the next modality period, issuer default payment methods), emails the client the branded message with the PDF attached and stamps billing_requested_at (pauses the expiry notices; a 'Cobro enviado' badge appears). Partial failure (email down) keeps the document issued and warns to re-send from Cobros. La confirmación exige origen operativo explícitamente asociado al único hosting del proyecto y, si existe suscripción, una obligación existente seleccionada. Los orígenes pendientes bloquean emitir; permite navegar a conciliación administrativa antes de enviar.

admin-accounting-hosting-client.name: Admin Accounting Hosting Client Link
admin-accounting-hosting-client.description: Every hosting belongs to a client, so the hosting form carries a searchable client picker with inline creation and requires it on NEW records. Records saved before the relation kept the client as free text following the house convention "Persona - Marca": opening one searches that text and offers the matching registered client for confirmation (accent- and case-blind, both halves tried against name and company), while a still-unlinked record is flagged as pending and stays saveable — completing it is a separate step. The table shows the client with a "sin vincular" pill, the filter panel gains a Cliente filter with a "Sin cliente" sentinel, a builtin tab isolates the pending group, and a header card counts it. Rows are completed in bulk from the shared ClientBulkAssignBar, the same component /panel/accounting/incomes uses: The bulk bar holds only the selection count and one [Acciones] menu; Asignar cliente and Asignar proyecto open BulkAssignModal (picker + live plan + gated confirm), Desvincular cliente and Quitar proyecto go straight to the confirmation, and Registrar abono opens its own modal. The menu opens upward (the bar is sticky at the bottom) and separates linking from collecting with a divider; Headless UI only renders the panel while it is open, so an action being absent or disabled is only observable with the menu open. "Asignar cliente" opens the modal, whose confirm stays disabled while no client is picked with the reason on the line right beside it — an empty picker no longer means unlink — and "Desvincular cliente" only appears in the menu when a selected row actually has a client. Either way the scope is named before anything is written: how many rows gain a client, how many change one and from which client (a mixed selection is broken down instead of presented as a single operation), plus the full scrollable list of affected records. Only the rows that actually change travel in POST /api/accounting/hostings/bulk-assign-client/ (one audit entry per hosting), and the toast afterwards reports how many the server really wrote. Selecting a client seeds the billing snapshot without overwriting what the operator typed. The cuenta de cobro then inherits the client: the send action gates on the resolved recipient (hosting override, else the client address) instead of a hosting-only email, issues on that client's PA-{CODE}-{NNN} series and links the document to the client user. A client holding hostings can no longer be deleted, and the client card lists their hostings with the monthly total alongside their incomes. (Ago 2026) Selection reconciliation is shared with incomes: deleting a selected hosting drops its id alone, the bar hides itself when the selection empties, and a bulk assign naming a hosting that no longer exists is refused with 409 records_not_found instead of writing the surviving half of the batch.

admin-accounting-hosting-cycles.name: Admin Accounting Hosting Cycle Payments
admin-accounting-hosting-cycles.description: Superuser registers hosting cycle payments from the row menu's 'Ciclos de pago' entry at /panel/accounting/hostings: the modal shows immutable historical modality/amount snapshots and a register form offering quarterly, semiannual and every-9-month cycles. It is prefilled from the current contract (amount = payment_per_cycle, modality, paid_at = today) with an 'Extender vigencia' toggle. total_paid/cycles_count recompute from history; deleting a cycle recalculates but never rolls back valid_to.

admin-accounting-hosting-inline-edit.name: Admin Accounting Hosting Inline Edit
admin-accounting-hosting-inline-edit.description: Superuser edits hosting cells without opening the modal at /panel/accounting/hostings: double-click on cliente, dominio or valor/mes swaps the cell for an input (money cells use BaseCurrencyInput), Enter/blur PATCHes only when the value changed, Esc cancels; a failed PATCH leaves the row untouched. The estado column is an inline select that PATCHes is_active with snap-back and spinner.

admin-accounting-hostings.name: Admin Accounting Hostings
admin-accounting-hostings.description: Superuser manages the client hosting registry at /panel/accounting/hostings: list with an inline estado select, validity, 4 KPI cards and modal CRUD. New records offer exactly quarterly, semiannual and every-9-month payment modalities, with payment_per_cycle derived from the monthly value. Legacy monthly/annual rows remain readable as historical values but cannot be selected for new records. Ciclos/total pagado are read-only in the form. Cliente renders the linked relation and Proyecto is a column of its own. Every row leads with a single three-dots control at every width (after the selection checkbox): its menu opens with Detalle e historial and Ver nota (when present), then cycles, cuenta de cobro, emails, edit and delete, and the estado cell wraps so the billing chip never pushes the row past a phone's edge. On a phone Valor/mes groups under Cliente so the row fits without a horizontal scroll. At 412×915, 835×1195, 1195×835, 1440×900 and 2560×1440, validity dates remain complete, may wrap between dates and never overlap the cycle count; grouped values stay accessible and the count still opens that hosting’s history. IVA (2026-10): IVA editable del pago por ciclo, 19% al crear y null histórico. Total incluido por defecto o base antes del impuesto; las siguientes cuentas heredan el porcentaje y muestran el desglose sin recalcular ciclos históricos.

admin-accounting-income-bulk-settle.name: Admin Accounting Income Bulk Settle
admin-accounting-income-bulk-settle.description: The selection bar shows selected original and pending totals, and Liquidar opens the same IncomeLiquidateModal as the individual action. It lists selected expected company incomes, proposes oldest-first coverage, accepts manual cash allocation and recalculation, and offers a global received amount, destination and Carlos/Gustavo split. A shortfall automatically opens Diferencia for proportional classified deductions and source-linked follow-up expected incomes. Unallocated balances remain pending; zero received is valid with a deduction or follow-up. IVA is a display-only inherited breakdown per income. The form previews POST /api/accounting/incomes/settlement-preview/ before one final POST /api/accounting/incomes/bulk-settle/. Confirmation choices and final review stay inside the same modal. Same-client excess becomes credit; mixed-client credit and invalid distributions are blocked. Preview/server failures preserve the form, and post-commit email failures warn without reversing money. Pocket movements retain their detail with allocation amounts and current balances; income payment links expose the sibling allocations of a shared abono.

admin-accounting-income-client.name: Admin Accounting Income Client Link
admin-accounting-income-client.description: Superuser links each income to the client it came from at /panel/accounting/incomes. The income form carries a searchable client picker (with inline client creation) and an Origen control for the business line (desarrollo/hosting/diagnostico/otro); the client is optional, so a refund or a financial yield can stay unassigned. The table shows a Cliente column, the filter panel gains Cliente (options derived from the loaded rows plus a "Sin cliente" sentinel) and Origen filters, and a "Sin cliente" builtin tab isolates the rows still to be completed. Those rows are completed in bulk from the shared ClientBulkAssignBar, the same component /panel/accounting/hostings uses: checkboxes select rows (or every filtered row) and The bulk bar holds only the selection count and one [Acciones] menu; Asignar cliente and Asignar proyecto open BulkAssignModal (picker + live plan + gated confirm), Desvincular cliente and Quitar proyecto go straight to the confirmation, and Liquidar opens its own modal. The menu opens upward (the bar is sticky at the bottom) and separates linking from collecting with a divider; Headless UI only renders the panel while it is open, so an action being absent or disabled is only observable with the menu open. "Asignar cliente" opens the modal, whose confirm stays disabled while no client is picked with the reason on the line right beside it — an empty picker no longer means unlink — and "Desvincular cliente" only appears in the menu when a selected row actually has a client. Either way the scope is named before anything is written: how many rows gain a client, how many change one and from which client (a mixed selection is broken down instead of presented as a single operation), plus the full scrollable list of affected records. Only the rows that actually change travel in POST /api/accounting/incomes/bulk-assign-client/ (one audit entry per income), and the toast afterwards reports how many the server really wrote. A "Totales por cliente" modal breaks the FILTERED incomes down into billed / collected / pending / weight per client with a totals row, so the period comes from the active filters. Settling an income carries its client and origin into the liquid child, and a client holding incomes can no longer be deleted. The list can also render GROUPED BY CLIENT: the backend setting income_default_view_mode (edited in Configuración) decides the landing mode on every visit, the in-page Agrupado/Clásico segmented toggle lasts only the session (nothing persists on the device), and the grouped table shows per-client headers over the whole filtered set with a trailing 'Sin cliente' bucket flagged 'por completar' and billed/collected/pending footer totals. Each group header reads as ONE UNIT at the start of the row: the client name with its record count and, contiguous to it, Facturado, Pendiente and Participación en lo facturado — each its own block with the label above the value in smaller muted type, so the name keeps the visual weight. That two-line block is what made the figures legible; spreading them across the width of the row was tried and rejected, because on a wide table the amounts landed far enough from the name to read as columns of something else again. The separation between the three blocks is uniform and compact with no separators (each already carries its own label), and the name and its count are centred against the two-line blocks. A long client name yields space and ellipsizes instead of pushing a figure out of the row or breaking one in half; the amounts never compress. The footer takes the same treatment, so the table reads the same way top to bottom — it keeps the order Facturado, Pendiente, Cobrado — which costs the vertical alignment between rows on purpose, since every name measures differently. Both amounts always render, zero included; the share label states what the figure IS (the group's part of the billed total, not how much of the group is billed); and below sm the blocks drop together to a second line under the name without stretching or breaking. Since Ago 2026 the grouped view also carries the selection: a checkbox per row, one per client group that ticks or clears the whole group and reads indeterminate while only part of it is selected, and a header 'seleccionar todos' spanning every group — with no pagination here, that is exactly the filtered set. A collapsed group states how many of its rows are selected, because they keep counting towards the bulk action; the selection lives on the page, so it survives switching between Agrupado and Clásico; and the same ClientBulkAssignBar drives the same two actions, now sticky at the bottom (incomes and hostings alike) and flagging '· N fuera del filtro actual' when part of the selection no longer passes the active filters — the action still includes those rows and the confirmation lists them. Pagination stays classic-only, while sorting is shared: Mes opens newest-first and toggles oldest/newest; Total cycles highest/lowest/default Mes order. In grouped mode the selected order applies inside each client group without changing the billed-desc group ranking or the trailing Sin cliente bucket. The active sort survives filters, quick tabs, view changes and later visits through browser storage. A 'Sin cliente' KPI card (without_client_count, whole filtered set) surfaces the completion debt, the search box also matches the linked client's name/company (server-side q included), each unassigned row in the classic table wears a 'sin vincular' pill, reassigning an expected's client cascades to its settled liquids, and the cuenta de cobro adopts the client on an orphan income or rejects a mismatched one. (Ago 2026) The selection is reconciled against the records that still exist: deleting a selected income drops that id on its own — only that one, so a partial deletion of a multi-selection keeps the rest — the count and the '· N fuera del filtro actual' notice recompute over real rows, and the bar hides itself once nothing is left to assign, with no reload and no Cancelar. If part of the batch was deleted while the confirmation was open, POST bulk-assign-client/ answers 409 records_not_found naming missing_ids and writes nothing; the panel drops those ids and reloads. The assignment modal opens with a permanent in-flow client catalog instead of a click-triggered dropdown: its A-Z/Z-A name order persists between openings, the search input filters the rows already in view, later pages load progressively in the catalog's only scrollbar, and an empty filter offers inline client creation. Name, company and email stay visible, missing email is called out, the modal never reserves blank dropdown height or scrolls behind the catalog, and the compact viewport uses the full screen. La barra de selección muestra valor total seleccionado y saldo pendiente seleccionado por separado; la liquidación no requiere cuenta emitida.

admin-accounting-income-crud.name: Admin Accounting Income CRUD
admin-accounting-income-crud.description: Superuser manages income records at /panel/accounting/incomes, a list that lands on the builtin "Solo esperados" tab (kind=expected + paymentStatus=pending) rather than on "Todas": create via modal with automatic 50/50 partner split (whole-peso halves, an odd peso or any cent staying in Bolsillo ProjectApp; editable, and a record whose split is not the automatic one opens with the toggle off), a period field that defaults to today's exact date with a month-only toggle (shared PeriodDateField; edits always open in full-date mode showing the stored day — 01 is the month-only storage sentinel — with the toggle still downgrading to month), ledger selector (Contabilidad: Empresa / Personal Gustavo / Personal Carlos — personal hides the split and pocket destination and uses a single Valor field) which is a filter only, with no column of its own since Aug 2026, edit with prefill (PATCH /api/accounting/incomes/:id/update/), delete with ConfirmModal (DELETE .../delete/), HTML5 required validation and backend error toasts via usePanelNotify. The list opens ordered by Mes from newest to oldest; Mes toggles newest/oldest, while Total cycles highest/lowest/default Mes order. The active order survives filters, quick tabs, Agrupado/Clásico changes and later visits through browser storage. Expected rows carry a fulfilment state in their own "Cobro" column, computed from their linked liquid records (Pagado green tint / Parcial amber tint with the outstanding amount inline / Pendiente untinted). Expected company rows also expose an independent forecast level and manual inclusion switch across list, create/edit form and detail; changing the color preserves the switch, neutral means 'Sin clasificar', and duplication clears both. They retain two extra row actions: 'Liquidar', which opens the same shared Liquidar ingresos modal used by multi-select, prefilled with the pending amount and today's exact payment date. Company settlements default to Bolsillo ProjectApp and show global Carlos/Gustavo amounts in the collapsed Participaciones header; personal settlements hide participation and destination. The form previews POST /api/accounting/incomes/settlement-preview/ before POST /api/accounting/incomes/bulk-settle/, even for one income. A lower received amount automatically opens Diferencia with its unassigned amount. Classified deductions and linked follow-up expected incomes can be combined; follow-ups name source, concept, month and amount. The unallocated remainder remains pending. Zero received is allowed with at least one deduction or follow-up, even if a remainder stays pending. The IVA section only shows inherited per-income breakdowns. Selected eligible client confirmations are reviewed inside the same modal before Confirmar y liquidar; a post-commit email failure warns without reversing the settlement.  Incomplete deduction or follow-up lines, negative or excessive allocations and invalid global partner amounts disable Liquidar with a persistent aria-live reason. No second adjustment form is opened. Deductions keep the expected income gross and count as payment credit via their source_income link; they reduce expected utility as real expenses (liquid utility already arrives net of them) and surface in the Gastos tab with a 'Descuento de ingreso' pill, a per-type filter and their own 'Naturaleza' filter, and 'Marcar como perdido', offered only on rows with no payments yet, which PATCHes kind=lost. Besides the landing tab the view ships two more builtin quick tabs: 'Hosting esperados' (the same cut plus the search term 'hosting', which seeds the search box) and 'Perdidos'; builtin tabs never drift, and '?accounting_incomeTab=all' opens the full list. Written-off income is a third kind, visible under 'Todos' and isolable via the builtin 'Perdidos' quick tab (or the 'Pérdidas' segment in the filter panel), with its own total chip and a 'Perdido (año)' KPI. Since Aug 2026 the row icons are a single three-dots button opening IncomeActionsModal (shared by the grouped and classic views, which had drifted apart), the Gustavo/Carlos columns moved into the income detail modal, and a Proyecto column joins Cliente. Since Aug 2026 every row also offers 'Duplicar' — available whatever the state, since the frequent case is reopening the next period of an already collected hosting — and the same action sits in the income detail modal. It does not write: it GETs /api/accounting/incomes/:id/duplicate-draft/ and opens the income form seeded with the original's concept, amounts, split, ledger, client, project, origin and notes, always as 'Esperado' and never carrying the original's settlement links, cuenta de cobro, deductions, history or silenced reminders. The proposed date is the original's plus one hosting cycle when the hosting behind it can be resolved unambiguously (labelled as such under the field); otherwise it opens empty and the field's required blocks the save until a date is chosen. Because most of the book carries no origin and no client, that lookup resolves for almost no income, so the form also offers cadence shortcuts ('+1 mes', '+3 meses', '+6 meses', '+1 año') built server-side from the original's date: picking one fills the field (in month granularity when the exact-day toggle is off) and marks itself pressed, and it overrides the hosting proposal when the two disagree. While the draft is being fetched the row's three-dots button spins and refuses a second click, since the action menu closes on click. Confirming POSTs through the ordinary create endpoint, so the new row gets a row flash and an 'Ingreso duplicado' toast that reads apart from a manual alta; a failing draft only raises 'No se pudo preparar el duplicado'. Since Aug 2026 an income with Origen Hosting swaps the single date for the period it covers, laid out in the order it is filled: Periodicidad rides in the top row beside Tipo (it is chosen before the dates it proposes), and inicio and fin share the row below so the range reads left to right, with the exact-day toggle under inicio — the date it applies to — and the cadence shortcuts under both, followed by an independent 'Mes/Fecha de cobro esperado' that follows the start until edited and drives income ordering and payment reminders; edits and duplicate drafts preserve a payment date offset from the covered window. The Periodicidad catalog is the recurring-payments one and its hint says what it does for the user ('Al elegirla se calcula la fecha de fin del período'), not where the catalog came from. Picking a cadence recomputes immediately: it writes the inclusive end (start + cadence − 1 day, day clamped) and, when there is no start yet, opens the window on the period after the last one recorded — GET /api/accounting/incomes/period-suggestion/ resolves that antecedent by client, narrowed by project, and the start field states which period this one follows ('El período anterior terminó el …'); the first charge of a client falls back to today, and a client holding several active hostings with no project to tell them apart gets no proposal rather than a guessed one. Moving the start carries the end with it keeping the cadence, and writing the end by hand turns the cadence to 'Personalizada' instead of leaving the selector claiming a length the window no longer has; under 'Personalizada' both dates are written by hand and nothing recomputes. The recompute runs off the values themselves, so it also fires when the start is written programmatically — turning the origin to Hosting, or a shortcut. Switching the origin keeps everything already typed, but a create's untouched 'today' default is boilerplate rather than an answer and does not carry into the window, which is what lets the antecedent fill it. The cadence shortcuts ('+1 mes', '+3 meses', '+6 meses', '+1 año') are offered whenever a period is being OPENED — creating or duplicating, never while editing one already on the book — and each one anchors on the antecedent, so clicking several in a row re-lengthens the same window instead of walking a period further forward each time; the selector and the buttons stay in sync, with the pressed state reading back from both cadence and start. The three fields are required for hosting (creating and editing — legacy hosting rows complete their period on first edit), and fin must come after inicio, refused inline under the field before the submit as well as by the serializer. Other origins keep the single date, clearing any stray window, and their duplicate shortcuts still write the server-computed date. A duplicate always counts from the record it copies, never from today: the draft carries a period_anchor stating what it counted off, and the form anchors its own arithmetic on it. A recorded window proposes inicio = day after the recorded fin with the cadence's own length ('income_period'), and a legacy row falls back to the hosting-catalog lookup ('hosting_cycle'); both fix the inicio, so changing the periodicidad in the modal only moves the fin. When the original has neither -- no window and several active hostings to tell apart, which is the majority of the book -- the anchor is the original's own DATE ('original_date'): nothing is prefilled, because only the cadence can say how long that period lasted, and picking one opens the window where that period would have closed (fecha del original + periodicidad). That last anchor floats -- another cadence moves the whole window, since the fin it counts from is precisely what was never recorded -- while a start written by hand is never moved by a later cadence. A BaseAlert over the block says which of the three it was and names the dates, so a chained date is distinguishable from a guess; today is reached only when the original carries no date at all, and the notice says the range chains with nothing. The recorded window also rides into the cuenta de cobro as the pre-filled 'Período facturado', and the income export appends Período inicio / Período fin / Periodicidad columns. (Ago 2026) Origen is required on every income the form writes -- creating, editing and duplicating alike: BaseSegmented carries no native required, so the form refuses with 'Elige la linea de negocio del ingreso.' from the first submit attempt on, and the write serializer enforces the same on create and on any update that writes the field (a partial PATCH that does not touch it leaves a legacy row as unclassified as it was; settling is exempt, since the liquid child and the rescheduled balance copy the parent's line of business, blank included). Duplicating inherits origin like every other field that governs the shape of the form (origin, ledger, period_cadence; kind and destination are the declared overrides), so a hosting duplicate opens on the covered-window block and the other three lines on the single date. The copy is faithful rather than helpful: an original with no origin -- most of the book, which predates the field -- opens a duplicate with none, and a BaseAlert under the control says so ('El ingreso original no tiene origen registrado...') instead of letting a silent blank read as a copy that failed. The leading three-dots menu opens with Detalle e historial (the detail modal, which carries the record history) and Ver nota when the income has one; its kebab keeps the 44 px target. IVA (2026-10): IVA opcional: ingresos nuevos de cualquier contabilidad usan 19%; cambiar de contabilidad conserva la tasa elegida y editar respeta el valor histórico; se captura total incluido por defecto o base antes del impuesto. El formulario y detalle muestran base, IVA y total; 0 significa Sin IVA y null histórico conserva IVA sin registrar. La cuenta emitida o los pagos impiden cambiar el IVA. Reparto y utilidad conservan sus reglas. Liquidación unificada (2026-10-19): un esperado de empresa con saldo se puede Liquidar sin cuenta emitida, desde la acción individual o múltiple, en un solo modal con Participaciones, Diferencia e IVA colapsables. Al quedar pagado conserva Cuenta pendiente de emitir y las acciones para generar o completar la cuenta. La confirmación por ingreso elegible se revisa en el mismo modal; el envío sale después del commit y sus fallos se reintentan desde Historial sin repetir el abono.

admin-accounting-income-reminder-mute.name: Admin Accounting Income Reminder Mute
admin-accounting-income-reminder-mute.description: A superuser can silence the payment-calendar reminders of one uncollected expected income from its row menu, either until a future date or indefinitely. The Cobro cell shows the muted state and its resume date, so a deliberately quiet receivable cannot look unmonitored. A muted row offers Reactivar avisos, which clears both mute fields immediately. The modal rejects empty or non-future resume dates, and an API failure keeps the modal open and the row unchanged. Only expected, not-fully-paid incomes expose the action; the dedicated POST /api/accounting/incomes/:id/mute/ endpoint audits the change without generating another accounting email.

admin-accounting-list-error-retry.name: Admin Accounting Lists — Load Error & Retry
admin-accounting-list-error-retry.description: When a GET /api/accounting/<entity>/ (or dashboard/, change-logs/, settings/) fails, the page replaces the table/summary with AccountingErrorState (data-testid=accounting-error-retry): a Spanish danger alert plus a Reintentar button that re-fires the page's load function. CRUD errors keep using toasts and never hide the table. Mirrors admin-diagnostic-list-error-retry.

admin-accounting-pocket.name: Admin Accounting Pocket Ledger
admin-accounting-pocket.description: Superuser manages the ProjectApp pocket ledger at /panel/accounting/pocket: balance card from list meta, running-balance column (default view newest-first). The pocket is the money entry point: creating a movement also creates its linked income (IN) or expense (OUT). A new movement opens on Egreso, the common case, with every direction-dependent field already in its egreso variant; editing keeps the direction the record has. For IN the Contabilidad segmented is company-only; for OUT the selector is relabeled 'Atribuir a' (Empresa/Gustavo/Carlos) because pocket money is company money: every OUT mirrors a company-ledger expense that counts against liquid utility — Empresa splits 50/50, a partner option registers a draw fully assigned to that partner (category personal). Linked movements open the edit modal with the direction locked and the attribution prefilled (derived from the split); edits mirror into the linked record and deletes cascade both ways (confirm warns about the cascade). Unlinked historical movements keep plain CRUD. Since Aug 2026 the filter panel exposes every field the movement form captures (the 'insumo' criterion): on top of Fecha, Tipo and Valor it carries 'Atribuir a' (multi: Empresa/Gustavo/Carlos, over the mirror-derived `linked_ledger`) and 'Vínculo' (Todos/Vinculados/Sin vincular, over `is_auto_managed` — the way to find movements that never got their mirror), while the free-text fields ride the search box, which now covers `notes` as well as `concept`. Both new cuts exist server-side too (a `q_filters` knob on the shared filter layer), so the CSV export and the MCP `list_pocket` return the same rows the table shows, and the export gained 'Atribución' + 'Vinculado' columns. Because the running balance is a chronological accumulation, it is computed AFTER filtering: with any filter active the column is relabeled 'Acumulado' and sums only the visible rows, the subtitle says so, and the balance card — which the server always computes over every movement — is labeled '(total, no refleja los filtros)' and gains a 'N movimientos filtrados · neto X' line. The saved-tab strip (ProposalFilterTabs, the PA-44 standard) ships six seeded cuts — Entradas, Salidas, Gustavo, Carlos, Empresa, Sin vincular (migration accounts/0050 backfills them for existing users) — each with its count in parentheses, the honest (0) included, computed in the browser via `countTabs` since the whole dataset is already in the store; what does not fit the strip collapses into the '+N' overflow menu. Under the panel responsive contract, widths below 640 px stop rendering an eight-column table and render one semantic card per movement instead: a leading 44×44 action opens the row menu (Detalle e historial, Ver nota when the movement has one, Editar, Eliminar), concept and signed value lead the card, and date, atomic type/link badges and Saldo después (or Acumulado filtrado) follow as labelled facts. Those cards preserve sorting without horizontal scroll or overlap; from 640 px the priority table returns with the same leading action, the independent balance column returns at landscape width, module and saved-filter strips become selectors below 1024 px, and the 1400 px shell ceiling keeps the ledger coherent on a 2560 px monitor. The copy button next to Saldo del bolsillo writes the displayed total with currency symbol and Colombian separators, independent of movement filters. It reports local success or clipboard failure and is disabled while the total is loading or unavailable. Each row also names its owner (Empresa, Gustavo, Carlos or Sin vincular). A query-addressed compact detail (`?movement=<id>`) presents its monetary value, human-readable date and type, the real post-movement balance (distinct from a filtered table's Acumulado), owner, notes, linked income or expense, and allocation rows with each income's current outstanding amount or explicit customer credit. Linked expenses open with `?expense=<id>` even when list filters exclude them; the detail retains its history tab and gives a retryable failure state.

admin-accounting-project-bulk-assign.name: Admin Accounting Project Bulk Assign
admin-accounting-project-bulk-assign.description: The bulk bar holds only the selection count and one [Acciones] menu; Asignar cliente and Asignar proyecto open BulkAssignModal (picker + live plan + gated confirm), Desvincular cliente and Quitar proyecto go straight to the confirmation, and Registrar abono opens its own modal. The menu opens upward (the bar is sticky at the bottom) and separates linking from collecting with a divider; Headless UI only renders the panel while it is open, so an action being absent or disabled is only observable with the menu open. Asignar proyecto opens a catalog-wide combobox (every project, searched by name or client, actives first) and the confirmation shows the exact plan before anything runs: who gains the project, who changes project (origins named), who is already there, and - the bucket the client flavour does not have - the rows of ANOTHER client the ownership rule refuses to touch (blocked, never in the payload; the backend enforces the same rule with 409 client_mismatch/mismatched_ids and the page drops exactly those ids). Quitar proyecto is its own destructive action, clearing is allowed across clients (removing a link needs no owner), and the response rows rebuild the table in place - cascaded liquid children included on incomes. The client bulk preview now also announces which rows will lose their project when the client changes hands.

admin-accounting-project-coherence.name: Admin Accounting Client/Project Coherence
admin-accounting-project-coherence.description: Requisito 14 of the coherence ticket, verified end to end over a stateful mock backend: changing the client of a hosting announces the project side effect in the preview (the project belonged to the previous client, so the move clears it), rebuilds the row in place from the mutation response (client cell, "sin proyecto" marker), moves the per-project counters that /panel/projects reads, and - after a full page.reload() - serves the exact same truth from the backend state: the database is the source of coherence and the reload never was what fixed the view.

admin-accounting-project-hosting-reconci.name: Admin Accounting Project Hosting Reconciliation
admin-accounting-project-hosting-reconci.description: Inventaría y asocia explícitamente suscripción y orígenes contables al único hosting del proyecto, elige origen operativo y concilia referencias financieras con preview, motivo y versión. No registra dinero ni elige por texto o importe.

admin-accounting-receivables.name: Admin Accounting Receivables Forecast
admin-accounting-receivables.description: Superuser controls a global manual collection forecast from the 'Pendiente por cobrar' card on /panel/accounting. The card total is the sum of original amounts for selected, open, expected company incomes classified green/high. Its modal reads GET /api/accounting/receivables/ and exposes three tabs: totals and rows grouped by green/high, orange/medium, red/low and unclassified; a flat selected summary; and management of all open expected company candidates. Candidate management opens grouped by client, can regroup by project or switch to a classic flat list, and shows original, paid and open totals for each group. This presentation resets to client grouping whenever the modal opens. Candidate toggles and traffic-light confidence changes PATCH independently, assigning a color preserves the manual switch, and a failed request leaves a visible retry action. Floating help remains inside the modal overlay so its complete traffic-light legend is readable. A soft circle accompanies the full green/high, orange/medium, red/low or neutral/unclassified label in the modal, expected-income list, create/edit form and income detail.

admin-accounting-record-history.name: Admin Accounting Record Change History
admin-accounting-record-history.description: Abre Detalle e historial o Ver historial de cambios desde ingresos, gastos, hosting, recurrentes, bolsillo, Ads, tarjetas, extractos, movimientos, alias, destinatarios, cuentas de cobro y configuración. El historial presenta fecha, autor, origen y cambios; carga 20 entradas por página. Evidencia antigua incompleta no se puede comparar. Errores de carga, consulta o comparación permiten reintentar. En todas las tablas y listas contables, Detalle e historial es la primera opción del menú de tres puntos de la fila (en ingresos y cuentas de cobro abre su detalle, que incluye el historial): la columna de acciones sólo aloja ese botón.

admin-accounting-recurring.name: Admin Accounting Recurring Payments
admin-accounting-recurring.description: Superuser manages recurring operational costs at /panel/accounting/recurring. Vigentes and Archivados are separate scopes; only active, non-archived rows contribute to monthly totals, participation percentages, charts and upcoming-charge notices, and the interface says so explicitly. In both grouped and classic views a leading three-dots control owns the row actions: detail and history; its note when it has one; edit; duplicate through a non-persisted, prefilled draft whose next charge is recalculated; activate/deactivate; mute or resume reminders; and archive. Archived rows preserve their data, can be restored as inactive, and expose permanent deletion only after typed confirmation. Grouped and classic tables support multi-selection for atomic activate, deactivate and archive actions; duplicate remains one row at a time. The existing category catalog, drag ordering, monthly normalization, currency conversion and category drill-down remain available, while charts always use the budget scope and no longer offer an inactive-row toggle. Registering a real expense/pocket movement and browsing charge history remain a separate accounting-origin scope rather than being inferred by this lifecycle change.

admin-accounting-settings-reset-tabs.name: Admin Accounting Settings — Reset Saved Filter Tabs
admin-accounting-settings-reset-tabs.description: Superuser restores the seeded default filter tabs per accounting view from /panel/accounting/settings: the 'Pestañas de filtros guardados' card lists the 6 views (Ingresos/Gastos/Hostings/Bolsillo/Recurrentes/Ads) each with a Restablecer button that, after a ConfirmModal warning about custom tabs, POSTs accounts/saved-filter-tabs/reset/ (delete + re-seed atomically) and toasts the result.

admin-accounting-settings.name: Admin Accounting Settings
admin-accounting-settings.description: Superuser configures accounting email notifications at /panel/accounting/settings. The recipient list is its own catalog (GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/accounting/notification-recipients/, audited): every row shows the address, whether it is Activo or Pausado and its fecha de alta; adding validates the format and rejects duplicates case-insensitively with the error inline; a per-row switch pauses a recipient without deleting it; each row leads with a three-dots menu (Detalle e historial, Ver nota, Quitar) and removing asks for confirmation naming the automations that stop arriving. Each row saves on its own, not through the page's save button. Every automated email of the module — change notices, card-debt and statement reminders, the payment calendar, cuentas de cobro and hosting payment outcomes — goes to the active recipients and to nobody else. The master switch (notifications_enabled, PATCH /api/accounting/settings/update/) pauses all of it at once; with it off, or with zero active recipients, the panel warns explicitly that nobody is being notified. Also hosts the weekly card-debt reminder toggle (Fridays 9:00 Bogotá, re-alert every 2 days until the snapshot is registered), the statement reminder toggle (every 8 days at 9:05 Bogotá while the previous month's statement of an active catalog card is missing, draft or lacks its PDF), the 'Catálogo de tarjetas' section (see admin-accounting-card-catalog), the hosting expiry notices toggle (15/7 days before valid_to, then every 5 days until the cuenta de cobro is sent), the USD exchange rate used by the recurring USD KPI, the 'Vista de ingresos' segmented control (income_default_view_mode: whether /panel/accounting/incomes lands grouped by client or as the classic table on every visit; the in-page toggle is session-only), and the globally persisted Cuentas de cobro view/criterion pair (grouped or classic, client or project), which can also be saved immediately from that list.

admin-accounting-statements.name: Admin Accounting — Credit Card Statements
admin-accounting-statements.description: Superuser reviews the monthly credit-card statement ledger at /panel/accounting/statements: backend-driven year options (from the catalog's statements_since; months before it show 'No aplica') + card filters over a 12-month grid (Procesado/Borrador/Pendiente chips per card), inline statement detail (totals stat cards, category bars, transactions table flagging unidentified lines, 'Documento del extracto' PDF block with upload/view/replace/delete), finalize with forced-close confirm on total mismatch (POST /api/accounting/statements/:id/finalize/), reopen, delete, header edit modal and manual add-transaction on drafts, per-line delete on drafts, and single-click inline editing of fecha/descripcion/comercio/categoria/cuota/valor directly in the table (dashed underline + hover pencil as the affordance): comercio is a combobox over the learned merchant catalog that offers to remember the alias afterwards (POST /api/accounting/merchant-aliases/learn/) and can carry its default category, cuota is captured as a structured number/total pair, and negative amounts (refunds) edit inline keeping their sign. Editing a processed statement is allowed through a reopen-and-edit confirmation, since the backend keeps refusing writes on non-draft statements. Also: the per-line modal covering fecha, descripcion, comercio, categoria, cuota, valor and notas, and a 'Copiar prompt' button for the MCP chat kick-off. The collapsible 'Comercios aprendidos' table below the detail carries the same single-click inline editing over texto a mapear / comercio / categoria (PATCH /api/accounting/merchant-aliases/:id/update/, which re-normalizes the descriptor and rejects one already owned by another alias) plus per-row delete. Statements are normally created from the claude.ai chat via the accounting MCP connector (create_statement). Each transaction and learned-merchant row leads with a three-dots menu: Detalle e historial, Ver nota when present, Editar for transactions and Eliminar (only while the statement is a draft for transactions); below 1024 px the kebab leads each card.

admin-accounting-stats-modals.name: Admin Accounting Statistics Surfaces
admin-accounting-stats-modals.description: Superuser opens descriptive-statistics surfaces from the accounting Resumen. Ingresos líquidos, Gastos {year} and Deuda tarjetas remain clickable cards that open StatsModal (BaseModal 5xl + BaseTabs) with their tabbed ApexCharts views. Utility statistics no longer use an icon or modal: evolution, margins and partner distribution are embedded inside the Utilidad líquida hero as a default-open accordion. Income/expense tabs feed from GET /api/accounting/stats/?year= (lazy, cached per year in the accounting store and reset on year change); utility/cards views compute client-side from the dashboard summary and card snapshots.

admin-additional-modules-catalog.name: Admin Additional Modules Catalog
admin-additional-modules-catalog.description: Admin navigates from the panel sidebar, switches the bilingual catalog between Spanish and English, uses card, list or accordion mode, and can retry a failed catalog load.

admin-additional-modules-explainer-visib.name: Admin Additional Modules Explainer Visibility
admin-additional-modules-explainer-visib.description: Admin shows or hides the catalog explainer video for clients from the panel switch next to the compact card; the change is confirmed, and a failed save puts the switch back with an error.

admin-additional-modules-explainer.name: Admin Additional Modules Explainer
admin-additional-modules-explainer.description: Admin previews the catalog explainer video from the compact card on the additional modules panel page. Playback starts only after a click, pauses when the page or window loses activity, and never resumes automatically on return.

admin-additional-modules-manage.name: Admin Manage Additional Modules
admin-additional-modules-manage.description: Admin creates or edits a bilingual module, receives local validation for incomplete content, and sees server save failures in the form.

admin-additional-modules-pdf.name: Admin Download Additional Modules PDF
admin-additional-modules-pdf.description: Admin selects modules, language and an optional client recipient, downloads the personalized PDF, and gets a visible failure message if generation fails.

admin-additional-modules-quick-access.name: Admin Additional Modules Quick Access
admin-additional-modules-quick-access.description: Admin sees and copies the canonical public catalog URL, downloads the complete active catalog PDF in one click, and uses dashboard metrics and shortcuts to prepare a tracked client selection.

admin-additional-modules-reorder.name: Admin Reorder Additional Modules
admin-additional-modules-reorder.description: Admin changes category or module order and receives a recoverable message when the optimistic catalog revision is stale.

admin-additional-modules-share-video.name: Admin Additional Modules Share Link Video
admin-additional-modules-share-video.description: Admin creates a shared catalog link without the explainer video, turns it back on for one link from the history, and sees that no link shows the video while the catalog switch hides it.

admin-additional-modules-share.name: Admin Share Additional Modules Selection
admin-additional-modules-share.description: Admin selects relevant modules, validates the recipient, generates a public link, and reviews or revokes tracked links.

admin-admin-management.name: Admin User Management
admin-admin-management.description: Manage admin users: list with status filters (All/Active/Inactive), invite new admin via modal, view and deactivate existing admins.

admin-auto-archive-zombie.name: Admin Auto-Archive Zombie Proposals
admin-auto-archive-zombie.description: System auto-archives expired proposals with no activity in 30 days.
knownGaps: Backend-only, covered by backend unit tests

admin-blog-calendar.name: Admin Blog Calendar
admin-blog-calendar.description: Weekly calendar view showing scheduled, published, and draft blog posts.

admin-blog-create-from-json.name: Admin Blog Create (JSON Import)
admin-blog-create-from-json.description: Create a blog post by importing a structured JSON payload with content_json sections, template download, validation, and preview.

admin-blog-create.name: Admin Blog Create (Manual)
admin-blog-create.description: Create a new bilingual blog post via manual form with category, readTime, featured, SEO fields.

admin-blog-edit.name: Admin Blog Edit
admin-blog-edit.description: Edit an existing blog post including new fields: category, readTime, isFeatured, content_json, SEO meta.

admin-blog-linkedin-connect.name: Admin Blog LinkedIn Connect
admin-blog-linkedin-connect.description: Admin connects LinkedIn account from blog post edit page via OAuth 2.0 popup flow. Popup opens at authorization URL, user authenticates, /auth/linkedin/callback exchanges code via POST /api/linkedin/callback/, popup notifies opener via postMessage, edit page updates to show connected profile.
knownGaps: OAuth popup requires real LinkedIn credentials — E2E should mock the callback URL and API endpoints

admin-blog-linkedin-publish.name: Admin Blog LinkedIn Publish
admin-blog-linkedin-publish.description: Admin fills LinkedIn summary (EN preferred or ES, ≤1300 chars), selects language (defaults to English — US market focus), clicks 'Publicar en LinkedIn' → POST /api/blog/admin/:id/publish-linkedin/. Success message renders. Publish button disabled when summary is empty. Last publish timestamp shown after success.

admin-blog-list.name: Admin Blog List
admin-blog-list.description: View the list of all blog posts (admin view with both languages).

admin-blog-overdue-detection.name: Admin Blog Overdue Schedule Safety-Net
admin-blog-overdue-detection.description: Backend Huey periodic task scans BlogPost rows where publish_scheduled_for is in the past but the post is still unpublished, then publishes them automatically (and triggers the LinkedIn auto-publish if connected). The management command publish_blog_post.py is a manual escape hatch for the same logic. No browser interaction.
knownGaps: Backend-only safety-net for missed schedules. Covered by backend/content/tests/tasks/test_blog_publish_guards.py; no E2E spec applies.

admin-blog-publish-mode.name: Admin Blog Publish Mode
admin-blog-publish-mode.description: From the blog edit page, admin selects how the post should be published via three radio options: 'Borrador' (draft), 'Publicar ahora' (immediate), or 'Programar' (scheduled). Selecting 'Programar' reveals a datetime input for publish_scheduled_for. If the STORED schedule (published_at at hydration time) is in the past, an amber overdue banner ([data-test='scheduled-overdue-banner']) warns that the safety-net Huey task will publish on the next run; the banner is not live input validation. The mode is computed by frontend/utils/blogPublishMode.js (resolveBlogPublishMode → { mode, scheduledIso, overdue }) and submitted to the blog update endpoint.
admin-blog-publish-mode.knownGaps: Spec added 2026-07-22 (QA campaign round 4): draft/schedule reveal, past-date overdue banner, scheduled hydration and the publish-now PATCH payload over mocked API.

admin-building-on-demand-contract.name: Admin Building on Demand Contract
admin-building-on-demand-contract.description: Abrir Contrato para leer su contenido y la copia del Gestor Documental sincronizada, desactualizada o sin inicializar; consultar el estado todavía no disponible, descargar PDF y reintentar un fallo del contrato.

admin-building-on-demand-economics.name: Admin Building on Demand Economics
admin-building-on-demand-economics.description: Abrir la pestaña Economía desde Células para consultar costos internos y horas de equilibrio por nivel y plazo; reintentar si la API no entrega los cálculos.

admin-building-on-demand-history.name: Admin Building on Demand History
admin-building-on-demand-history.description: Pulsar Ver más en el historial del programa para añadir la siguiente página de versiones; ante un fallo, reintentar la carga conservando las revisiones ya consultadas.

admin-building-on-demand-program.name: Admin Building on Demand Program
admin-building-on-demand-program.description: Entrar a Células desde Comercial, consultar la revisión y el conector MCP, copiar los enlaces públicos, descargar el PDF y cambiar el idioma de la vista previa; reintentar un fallo del resumen.

admin-building-with-us-contract.name: Admin Building with Us Contract
admin-building-with-us-contract.description: Abrir Contrato, consultar Markdown y el espejo sincronizado en ProjectApp/Contratos; leer la advertencia desactualizada o sin inicializar, descargar PDF y reintentar un fallo del contrato.

admin-building-with-us-distribution.name: Admin Building with Us Distribution
